model.name: Task
model.purpose: Governed, format-neutral context model for a Task as a trackable unit of work that can be requested, assigned, performed, constrained, completed, failed, cancelled, or recorded as never valid, independently of any one storage or interface projection.
model.scope_statement: WM-ACT-006 covers the identity, classification, assignment, authority, lifecycle, composition, temporal and spatial bounds, inputs and outputs, constraints, provenance, access, retention and interoperability of a Task instance and its binding to an optional Task definition. A Task is a managed work item that spans intent and execution tracking; it is not a project, work order, plan, calendar event, clinical procedure, one-way notification, process model, or compute orchestration unit.
in_scope: Business and technical identifiers for a Task instance and optional binding to a Task definition or protocol
Type, code, intent, priority, categories, beneficiary, focus object and human-readable description
Requester, requested performer, owner, actual performer, excluded owners, stakeholders and business administrators
Lifecycle status, business status, status reason, claim, release, start, stop, suspend, resume, delegate, forward, complete, fail, cancel, reject and entered-in-error paths
Parent, child and grouped tasks, checklist items, named inputs and outputs, attachments and linked resources
Requested, start, due, execution, completion, recurrence, reminder and last-modified times with event time distinct from observation or ingestion time
Location, required resources, restrictions, do-not-perform prohibitions, completion conditions, percent complete and outcome
Notes, relevant history, provenance of key transitions, confidentiality class, access exceptions, retention and deletion, and cross-standard alignment maps
out_of_scope: Project, programme or portfolio as the containing work system (WM-ACT-005)
Work order as the authorizing operational grouping (WM-ACT-007)
Plan or schedule as an independently versioned artifact (WM-ACT-008)
Calendar Event (iCalendar VEVENT) as a time-bounded occurrence rather than an action item
Clinical Procedure or other event that records a physical or mental change to a subject
One-way notifications that require no work by a recipient
BPMN, BPEL or XPDL process definitions as models of process, as distinct from a Task instance that may instantiate them
Person, Organization, Location, Asset or Evidence master records except by reference
Amazon ECS or other compute-orchestrator task as a runtime container, which is a homonym not a work-item Task

boundary_notes.distinction: A project contains and governs a set of tasks and work packages; this model records a single Task and an optional containing-project reference. ISO 21502 treats a work package as a group of activities with scope, deliverable, timescale and cost, which is coarser than a Task.
A work order authorizes and groups operational tasks. The Task records the work item being performed; it does not own work-order commercial, maintenance or fulfillment semantics.

A plan or schedule is independently versioned. A Task may instantiate or reference a plan, ActivityDefinition, BPMN process, or iCalendar recurrence, but does not store the plan as its identity. PROV-O models Plan as an entity used in a qualified association, not as the Task itself.

FHIR Task tracks a workflow step such as fulfilling or signing an order. A Procedure is an action intended to change the subject. Task and Procedure may exist in parallel; Task is not a substitute for the clinical event.

schema.org Action is an action performed by an agent upon an object, optionally producing a result. PROV Activity is something that occurs over a period of time and uses or generates entities. Task is the governed work-item record that may describe a potential, in-progress or completed Action or Activity; it is not every ephemeral action occurrence.

VTODO is an action-item or assignment and cannot nest inside another calendar component; VEVENT is an event. OASIS WS-HumanTask treats notifications as one-way, fire-and-forget human tasks. Notifications and events are sibling concepts, not Task instances.

sources.title: HL7 FHIR Release 5 Resource Task
sources.relevance: Normative healthcare Task resource covering scope, state machine, REST queue usage, focus versus basedOn, inputs and outputs, definition binding, suspend and resume of children, and boundaries with Procedure and Request resources.

sources.title: HL7 FHIR Release 5 Task Detailed Descriptions
sources.relevance: Element-level schema for identifier, instantiatesCanonical, instantiatesUri, basedOn, groupIdentifier, partOf, status, statusReason, businessStatus, intent, priority, doNotPerform, code, description, focus, for, encounter, requestedPeriod, executionPeriod, authoredOn, lastModified, requester, requestedPerformer, owner, performer, location, reason, restriction, input and output.

sources.title: HL7 FHIR ValueSet Task Status
sources.relevance: Required Task status codes: draft, requested, received, accepted, rejected, ready, cancelled, in-progress, on-hold, failed, completed, entered-in-error, with definitions used to ground lifecycle findings.

sources.title: schema.org Action
sources.relevance: Web vocabulary for an action performed by an agent and participants upon an object, with instrument, location, startTime, endTime, result, error, actionStatus and identifier, used as an alignment rather than a work-item schema.

sources.title: schema.org ActionStatusType
sources.relevance: Four-member action status enumeration: PotentialActionStatus, ActiveActionStatus, CompletedActionStatus, FailedActionStatus, documenting a coarser competing status set.

sources.title: RFC 5545 Internet Calendaring and Scheduling Core Object Specification, section 3.6.2 To-Do Component
sources.relevance: Normative VTODO as an action-item or assignment with required UID and DTSTAMP, optional CLASS, COMPLETED, DUE, DURATION, DTSTART, PERCENT-COMPLETE, PRIORITY, STATUS, SUMMARY, ORGANIZER, ATTENDEE, RELATED-TO, RRULE, ATTACH, RESOURCES, VALARM, and the non-nesting rule.

sources.title: RFC 5545 section 3.8.1.11 Status
sources.relevance: VTODO STATUS values NEEDS-ACTION, COMPLETED, IN-PROCESS and CANCELLED, documenting a four-state to-do machine distinct from FHIR and WS-HumanTask.

sources.title: OASIS Web Services Human Task (WS-HumanTask) Specification Version 1.1
sources.relevance: Human-task definition versus instance, generic human roles, composite and ad-hoc subtasks, routing patterns, rendering, timeouts and escalations, claim, release, delegate, forward, completion conditions, task history events, lean tasks, and the explicit exclusion of notifications as one-way tasks.

sources.title: Microsoft Graph v1.0 todoTask resource type
sources.version_or_date: Microsoft Graph v1.0, document date 2024-07-22, page updated 2025-12-03
sources.relevance: Personal and work-item Task API with id that changes when moved between lists, status notStarted/inProgress/completed/waitingOnOthers/deferred, importance, due/start/completed/reminder times, recurrence, checklistItems, linkedResources, attachments and ISO 8601 timestamps.

sources.title: OMG Business Process Model and Notation Specification Version 2.0.2
sources.relevance: Authoritative process-modeling standard that FHIR Task may instantiate via instantiatesUri. Used to bound Task instance against process-definition semantics; detailed BPMN Task-type taxonomy is not taken from this landing page and is recorded as a gap.

sources.title: PROV-O: The PROV Ontology
sources.relevance: Provenance ontology relating Activity, Entity, Agent, used, wasGeneratedBy, wasAssociatedWith, actedOnBehalfOf, startedAtTime, endedAtTime, Plan and qualified associations, used to ground Task provenance, performer responsibility and plan reference without conflating Task with PROV Activity.

sources.title: ISO 21502:2020 Project, programme and portfolio management — Guidance on project management
sources.relevance: Public terms define a work package as a group of activities with defined scope, deliverable, timescale and cost, used to keep Task finer-grained than work package and outside project-management method ownership. Full clauses beyond the public preview remain a paywalled evidence gap.

sources.title: RFC 3339 Date and Time on the Internet: Timestamps
sources.relevance: Normative timestamp profile requiring complete date and time of day with seconds and a numeric offset or Z, used as the Task time encoding rule and to separate event instants from later observation.

bundles.name: Identity and classification
bundles.description: How a Task is identified, named, typed, prioritized and distinguished from definitions, lists, projects and homonymous compute tasks.
bundles.rationale: Every operating surface begins with stable identity and a type or code. FHIR, iCalendar and Graph disagree on identifier stability, so identity rules must be explicit before lifecycle or composition.

layers.name: Identity keys
layers.description: Master-system identifiers, business identifiers, global IRIs and Dimension-assigned UUIDs or ULIDs for Task instances, plus human-readable naming.

findings.name: Task instance identifiers
findings.description: A Task instance needs a master-system identifier, optional additional business identifiers, and optionally a governed IRI. Dates are not identifiers. Microsoft Graph documents that todoTask id changes when the item is moved between lists, which conflicts with FHIR Resource.id immutability and iCalendar UID persistence.

questions.text: What is the authoritative master-system identifier for this Task instance, and which system assigns and guarantees it?
Which business identifiers, group or requisition identifiers, and governed global IRIs also denote this Task?
Does the identifier remain stable across list moves, versioning and system copies, or must a Dimension UUID or ULID be assigned as a persistent surrogate?

data_elements.name: Master-system identifier
data_elements.description: Identifier assigned by the system of record for the Task instance.

data_elements.name: Business identifiers
data_elements.description: Zero or more business identifiers such as FHIR Task.identifier.

data_elements.name: Group or requisition identifier
data_elements.description: Shared identifier tying Tasks authorized together, such as FHIR groupIdentifier.

data_elements.name: iCalendar UID
data_elements.description: Required UID when the Task is projected as VTODO.

data_elements.name: Governed global IRI
data_elements.description: Optional HTTP IRI for the Task as a web-addressable thing.

data_elements.name: Dimension UUID or ULID
data_elements.description: Persistent identifier assigned by the adopting Dimension when master-system identity is missing or unstable.

artifacts.name: Task identity record
artifacts.description: Serial identity document mapping master-system id, business ids, IRI and Dimension UUID or ULID, with stability notes.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Key by authoritative master-system identifier; add governed IRI then Dimension UUID or ULID. Never key by date.

findings.name: Descriptive identity and confidentiality class
findings.description: Human-readable name, description, categories and iCalendar CLASS distinguish the Task for people and access control without serving as identity.

questions.text: What title or summary and free-text description should a human or agent use to recognize this Task?
Which categories, tags or outlook-style labels classify this Task for queues and search?
Is the Task public, private or confidential, and what privacy rules follow from that class?

data_elements.name: Title or summary
data_elements.description: Short human-readable name; FHIR code text, Graph title or iCalendar SUMMARY.

data_elements.name: Description
data_elements.description: Free-text explanation of what is to be performed.

data_elements.name: Categories
data_elements.description: Classification labels such as iCalendar CATEGORIES or Graph categories.

data_elements.name: Confidentiality class
data_elements.description: iCalendar CLASS of PUBLIC, PRIVATE or CONFIDENTIAL, or an aligned access class.

artifacts.name: Task narrative
artifacts.description: Human-readable title, body and category set used in task lists and renderings.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Inherit the Task master-system identifier; version the narrative separately from identity.

layers.name: Type, intent and priority
layers.description: What kind of Task this is, how actionable it is, and how urgently it should be addressed relative to other work.

findings.name: Task type, intent and priority
findings.description: FHIR separates Task.code, immutable Task.intent (proposal, plan, order and related codes) and RequestPriority. iCalendar PRIORITY is an integer 0 to 9. Graph importance is low, normal or high. These scales align but do not conform.

questions.text: What type or code describes the work this Task involves, and from which coding system?
Is this Task a proposal, plan, order or other intent level, and is that intent immutable for this instance?
What priority applies, on which native scale, and how is it mapped to the Dimension canonical priority?

data_elements.name: Task type code
data_elements.description: Codeable type such as FHIR Task.code.

data_elements.name: Intent
data_elements.description: Actionability level; FHIR Task.intent is required and immutable.

data_elements.name: Priority
data_elements.description: Native priority code or integer plus mapping to a canonical scale.

data_elements.name: Task definition reference
data_elements.description: Canonical or external URI of the protocol, ActivityDefinition, BPMN, BPEL or written instructions this Task instantiates.

artifacts.name: Task definition binding
artifacts.description: Link from the Task instance to a formal definition or guideline, including whether the definition is FHIR-canonical or an external URI.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Identify the definition by its own master identifier or IRI; the Task instance keeps a reference, not a copy of the definition identity.

bundles.name: Assignment and authority
bundles.description: Who requested the Task, who may or must perform it, who is excluded, and what higher-level authorization or focus object the Task fulfills.
bundles.rationale: WS-HumanTask and FHIR both treat assignment and authorization as first-class operating concerns distinct from status. Without roles and basedOn versus focus, agents cannot claim, refuse or fulfill work safely.

layers.name: People and generic human roles
layers.description: Requester, owner, requested and actual performers, potential owners, excluded owners, stakeholders and business administrators.

findings.name: Requester, owner and performers
findings.description: FHIR distinguishes requester, requestedPerformer, owner and performer.actor with optional function. schema.org uses agent, participant and provider. Graph infers the user from the containing todoTaskList rather than storing owner.

questions.text: Who created or requested this Task, and may that party cancel it?
Who is currently responsible for managing execution, and is an owner still unidentified?
Which actors actually performed the Task, and in what function or role?
Which access-control rules depend on requester versus owner versus performer?

data_elements.name: Requester
data_elements.description: Creator or asker for the Task.

data_elements.name: Requested performers
data_elements.description: Kind of participant or specific participants that should perform the Task.

data_elements.name: Owner
data_elements.description: Party responsible for managing execution; may be absent at creation.

data_elements.name: Performers
data_elements.description: Actors who performed the Task, with optional function.

artifacts.name: Assignment record
artifacts.description: Current and historical assignment of requester, owner and performers.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Identify by Task master-system identifier plus assignment event identifier; do not use assignment time as the only key.

findings.name: Generic human roles and exclusions
findings.description: WS-HumanTask defines task initiator, stakeholders, potential owners, actual owner, excluded owners, business administrators and notification recipients. Potential owners claim to become actual owner. Excluded owners cannot reserve or start the Task. Stakeholders and administrators can escalate missed deadlines.

questions.text: Who are the potential owners, who is the actual owner, and by what claim or nomination did ownership become actual?
Which people or groups are excluded from becoming potential or actual owner?
Who are the task stakeholders and business administrators, and which administrative operations may they perform?

data_elements.name: Potential owners
data_elements.description: People or groups who may claim the Task.

data_elements.name: Actual owner
data_elements.description: Person actually performing the Task after claim; not assigned in the definition.

data_elements.name: Excluded owners
data_elements.description: People who cannot become potential or actual owner.

data_elements.name: Task stakeholders
data_elements.description: People ultimately responsible for oversight and outcome.

data_elements.name: Business administrators
data_elements.description: Definition-level administrators with stakeholder-equivalent operations.

artifacts.name: People assignment
artifacts.description: WS-HumanTask-style people query or literal assignment for generic human roles, including logical people groups.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Identify assignments by Task instance plus role name; evaluate people queries against a directory that is out of band.

layers.name: Authorization, focus and beneficiary
layers.description: Higher-level request that triggered the Task, the resource being acted on, and who benefits.

findings.name: Based-on authorization versus focus object
findings.description: FHIR basedOn is a higher-level authorization such as a CarePlan. focus is the request being fulfilled or resource being manipulated. They are never the same. for is the beneficiary. doNotPerform inverts the requested action within tight time or phase bounds.

questions.text: What higher-level authorization or request created this Task, if any?
What object, request or resource is this Task acting on, and must subtasks be used if more than one resource is manipulated?
Who benefits from the Task, and is the Task asking that the action not occur?

data_elements.name: Based-on authorizations
data_elements.description: Higher-level requests that triggered creation of the Task.

data_elements.name: Focus
data_elements.description: Request being fulfilled or resource being manipulated.

data_elements.name: Beneficiary
data_elements.description: Entity who benefits from performance, such as a patient.

data_elements.name: Encounter or context event
data_elements.description: Healthcare or other event during which the Task originated.

data_elements.name: Do not perform
data_elements.description: True if the Task prohibits the specified action.

data_elements.name: Action object
data_elements.description: schema.org object upon which the action is carried out.

artifacts.name: Fulfillment context
artifacts.description: Record linking basedOn, focus, beneficiary and prohibition flag for fulfillment Tasks.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Identify by Task master-system identifier; referenced requests keep their own master identifiers.

bundles.name: Lifecycle and operations
bundles.description: Status machines, rare terminal paths, and the operations that move a Task between states.
bundles.rationale: Primary sources publish incompatible status vocabularies. Agents must record native status, a mapped canonical state, reasons, and the operations that are legal in each state, including entered-in-error, waiting-on-others, deferred, failed, rejected and child-cascading suspend.

layers.name: Status machine
layers.description: Current workflow status, business status and reasons, with explicit alignment rather than claimed conformance.

findings.name: Workflow status and business status
findings.description: FHIR requires Task.status from a twelve-code set and allows a separate businessStatus. iCalendar VTODO has four STATUS values. schema.org has four ActionStatusType members. Graph has five taskStatus values including waitingOnOthers and deferred. Native codes are stored; mappings are alignments.

questions.text: What is the current native workflow status, from which source vocabulary, and what is the mapped canonical state?
What business-specific substate, if any, refines the workflow status?
Why is the Task in its current status, especially if held, failed, refused or deferred?
When did this status become true as an event, and when was that change observed or ingested?

data_elements.name: Native status
data_elements.description: Status code in the source vocabulary.

data_elements.name: Canonical state
data_elements.description: Dimension-mapped state used for cross-system queues. Not a claim of conformance to any one standard.

data_elements.name: Business status
data_elements.description: Domain substate such as specimen collected.

data_elements.name: Status reason
data_elements.description: Explanation for the current status.

data_elements.name: Status vocabulary
data_elements.description: Identifier of the native status system, for example FHIR task-status or iCalendar statvalue-todo.

artifacts.name: Status alignment map
artifacts.description: Declared mapping from native status codes to canonical states, with conflict notes.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Identify maps by source vocabulary, target vocabulary and map version, not by date alone.

layers.name: Rare lifecycle paths and operations
layers.description: Entered-in-error, reject before start, fail versus cancel, waiting-on-others, deferred, potential-only actions, child-cascading suspend, stop back to ready, claim, release, delegate, forward and escalation.

findings.name: Rare and terminal lifecycle cases
findings.description: FHIR allows entered-in-error for a Task that should never have existed, rejected before action, failed from error, cancelled from external force, on-hold, and stop from in-progress back to ready for reassignment. Suspending a Task suspends children; resuming resumes children. WS-HumanTask adds claim, release, delegate, forward, skip, timeouts and escalations. Graph adds waitingOnOthers and deferred. These paths are in scope even when unused by a Dimension.

questions.text: If the Task is terminal, was it completed, failed, cancelled, rejected, skipped, exited or entered-in-error, and what evidence supports that path?
Is work blocked waiting on others or deferred, and what unblocks it?
Which lifecycle operations are legal from the current state for this actor, including claim, release, start, stop, suspend, resume, delegate, forward, complete, fail and cancel?

data_elements.name: Terminal path
data_elements.description: How the Task ended, if it ended.

data_elements.name: Entered in error flag
data_elements.description: True if the Task should never have existed and is retained only because it may have been used.

data_elements.name: Waiting on others
data_elements.description: Graph waitingOnOthers or equivalent blocked state.

data_elements.name: Deferred
data_elements.description: Work postponed without cancellation.

data_elements.name: Child suspend cascade
data_elements.description: Whether suspend and resume cascade to children.

data_elements.name: Escalation policy
data_elements.description: Timeouts and escalation actions from the Task definition.

artifacts.name: Task lifecycle history
artifacts.description: Append-only history of state and data-change events, including WS-HumanTask task events and FHIR relevantHistory Provenance links.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Each event has its own identifier; the Task master-system identifier is the subject, not the event key. Event time and ingestion time are both stored.

bundles.name: Composition and context
bundles.description: How Tasks nest, group, checklist, link to plans and schedules, and relate to siblings without absorbing those siblings.
bundles.rationale: Known Vercy relations place Task under Project and Work order and pointing at Plan. FHIR partOf, groupIdentifier and Graph checklistItems and linkedResources supply the instance-level composition surface.

layers.name: Hierarchy, grouping and links
layers.description: Parent and child Tasks, requisition grouping, checklists, related calendar components and linked resources.

findings.name: Parent, child, group and checklist composition
findings.description: FHIR partOf is a hierarchical reference, usually 0..1. WS-HumanTask supports composite tasks by definition and ad-hoc subtasks at runtime, plus routing patterns and completion conditions over subtasks. VTODO cannot nest in another calendar component and instead uses RELATED-TO. Graph models sub-work as checklistItems inside a todoTask that is always contained in a todoTaskList.

questions.text: Which parent Task, project, work order or task list contains this Task, and is the containment strict?
Which child Tasks or checklist items decompose this Task, and what completion condition rolls them up?
Which related tasks, events, journals, plans or linked resources are associated, and with what relationship type?
If multiple people or subtasks are involved, what sequential, parallel or mixed routing pattern applies?

data_elements.name: Part of
data_elements.description: Parent Task references.

data_elements.name: Child tasks
data_elements.description: Subtasks created by definition or ad hoc.

data_elements.name: Checklist items
data_elements.description: Graph-style checklist items that are not independent Task instances.

data_elements.name: Related-to
data_elements.description: iCalendar RELATED-TO links to other VTODO, VEVENT or VJOURNAL components.

data_elements.name: Linked resources
data_elements.description: External sources tracked on the Task.

data_elements.name: Completion condition
data_elements.description: How composite or parallel work completes.

artifacts.name: Task breakdown
artifacts.description: Parent-child graph, checklist and grouping document for a composite Task.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Composite identity is the parent Task master-system identifier; children keep independent master identifiers except checklist items, which are subordinate.

bundles.name: Time, place and work content
bundles.description: When and where the Task should occur or did occur, recurrence and reminders, required resources, and named inputs and outputs.
bundles.rationale: Temporal and spatial context is operating data, not identity. RFC 3339 encodes instants. FHIR, iCalendar and Graph each separate requested windows from execution and from record modification.

layers.name: Schedule, recurrence, reminders and location
layers.description: Requested period, start, due, execution, completion, recurrence, alarms and principal location.

findings.name: Temporal bounds, recurrence and reminders
findings.description: FHIR requestedPeriod is when completion is desired; executionPeriod is when work actually started and ended; authoredOn is creation; lastModified must be greater than or equal to authoredOn. iCalendar separates DTSTART, DUE or DURATION, COMPLETED, CREATED, LAST-MOD and DTSTAMP, and allows RRULE; a VTODO without DTSTART and DUE is associated with each successive calendar date until completed. Graph provides start, due, completed, reminder and patternedRecurrence. Event time and observation time are stored separately.

questions.text: When should this Task start and be due, and in which time zone or offset?
When did execution actually start and end, when was the Task completed, and when were those facts observed or ingested?
Does the Task recur, and what reminder or VALARM triggers apply, including overdue behavior?

data_elements.name: Requested period
data_elements.description: Desired window for performance.

data_elements.name: Due at
data_elements.description: Instant or date when the Task is to be finished, RFC 3339 with seconds and offset or Z when a time is present.

data_elements.name: Execution period
data_elements.description: Actual start and end of work.

data_elements.name: Completed at
data_elements.description: Event time of completion.

data_elements.name: Authored on
data_elements.description: Creation observation time of the Task record.

data_elements.name: Last modified
data_elements.description: Last modification observation time; must not precede authored-on.

data_elements.name: Recurrence
data_elements.description: RRULE or patterned recurrence.

data_elements.name: Reminder
data_elements.description: Reminder instant or VALARM definition.

artifacts.name: Task schedule slice
artifacts.description: Requested, due, execution and reminder times plus recurrence, distinct from the independently versioned plan model.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Identify by Task master-system identifier plus schedule-slice version; recurrence instances are not identified by their occurrence date alone.

findings.name: Location and required resources
findings.description: Principal place of performance, schema.org location including virtual location, and equipment or resources needed.

questions.text: Where is this Task expected or observed to occur, including virtual locations?
What equipment or resources are required to perform the Task?
If a geographic point is recorded, what coordinates and datum identify that place?

data_elements.name: Location reference
data_elements.description: Principal physical location, used only when work is primarily within one Location.

data_elements.name: Location text or virtual location
data_elements.description: schema.org location as Place, PostalAddress, Text or VirtualLocation.

data_elements.name: Geographic point
data_elements.description: iCalendar GEO when present.

data_elements.name: Resources needed
data_elements.description: iCalendar RESOURCES or schema.org instrument.

findings.inline_only_rationale: Location and resource needs are references to sibling Location and Asset models plus short codes or geometry. No distinct Task-owned location artifact is required unless a Dimension elects to snapshot a map or floorplan against the Task.

layers.name: Inputs, outputs, restrictions and progress
layers.description: Named parameters consumed and produced, fulfillment restrictions, percent complete and outcomes.

findings.name: Inputs, outputs, restrictions and progress
findings.description: FHIR Task.input and Task.output are named parameters for automation. restriction.repetitions, restriction.period and restriction.recipient limit fulfillment of a focus request and are allowed only for fulfill Tasks with a focus. iCalendar PERCENT-COMPLETE tracks progress. schema.org result and error describe outcomes. WS-HumanTask defines possible outcomes and completion behavior over subtasks.

questions.text: Which named inputs must or may be present before the Task can complete, and which are missing?
Which named outputs or result were produced, and what error describes a failed action?
What fulfillment restrictions apply, what percent is complete, and which possible outcomes remain open?
Why does this Task need to be performed, as a code or referenced justification?

data_elements.name: Inputs
data_elements.description: Named input parameters and values.

data_elements.name: Outputs
data_elements.description: Named output parameters and values.

data_elements.name: Result
data_elements.description: schema.org result produced by the action.

data_elements.name: Error
data_elements.description: Cause of failure for failed actions.

data_elements.name: Fulfillment restriction
data_elements.description: Subset of a focus request this Task is asked to fulfill.

data_elements.name: Percent complete
data_elements.description: Progress integer 0 to 100.

data_elements.name: Possible outcomes
data_elements.description: Declared outcomes such as approve or reject.

data_elements.name: Reason
data_elements.description: Why the Task is needed.

artifacts.name: Task input-output payload
artifacts.description: Named inputs and outputs transferred between Tasks or to a parent process.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Payload versions are identified by Task master-system identifier plus payload version; individual attachments keep their own identifiers.

bundles.name: Evidence, access, retention and interoperability
bundles.description: Provenance of key transitions, notes, attachments, access exceptions, retention and deletion, and declared alignments to external Task vocabularies.
bundles.rationale: A Task that cannot show who changed it, who may see it, how long it is kept, or how it maps to FHIR, iCalendar, WS-HumanTask or Graph cannot be operated across Dimensions.

layers.name: Provenance, access and retention
layers.description: History, notes, attachments, confidentiality, audit, retention and crosswalks.

findings.name: Provenance, notes and attachments
findings.description: FHIR relevantHistory points at Provenance for key past transitions, not the current version. WS-HumanTask maintains task event history and ad-hoc comments and attachments. PROV-O associates the performing activity with agents, used entities, generated entities and optional Plan. Graph supports file attachments and open extensions.

questions.text: Who was associated with or attributed for each key Task change, and on whose behalf did they act?
What notes, comments, file attachments and renderings document work on this Task?
Is the recorded history complete enough to compute wait time, time in progress and time to completion, and where are the gaps?

data_elements.name: Relevant history
data_elements.description: References to Provenance of key past versions.

data_elements.name: Notes
data_elements.description: Free-text annotations captured as the Task progresses.

data_elements.name: Attachments
data_elements.description: File or other attachments.

data_elements.name: Renderings
data_elements.description: WS-HumanTask rendering hints for user interfaces.

data_elements.name: Used entities
data_elements.description: PROV used entities consumed by the work.

artifacts.name: Task evidence pack
artifacts.description: Notes, attachments, renderings and provenance bundle for audit and quality metrics.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Evidence pack versions are identified independently of the Task; each binary attachment has its own master identifier and checksum.

findings.name: Access, retention and interoperability
findings.description: Who may read or change the Task, how long records and attachments are kept, when they are deleted or anonymized, and which external models are alignments only.

questions.text: Who may read, update, claim or administer this Task, and which confidentiality class or security labels apply?
How long is the Task and its attachments retained, and what deletion, anonymization or legal-hold exceptions apply?
Which external Task, to-do, human-task or action models is this instance aligned to, and which known conflicts remain unmapped?

data_elements.name: Security labels
data_elements.description: Confidentiality and handling labels, including iCalendar CLASS.

data_elements.name: Access policy reference
data_elements.description: Policy governing client operations on the Task.

data_elements.name: Retention period
data_elements.description: How long the Task record is kept after a terminal state.

data_elements.name: Legal hold
data_elements.description: Whether deletion is suspended.

data_elements.name: Alignment targets
data_elements.description: External model identifiers this Task is mapped to without claiming conformance.

artifacts.name: AGENTS.md bootstrap contract
artifacts.description: Mandatory agent bootstrap document declaring Name, Type, Specification URL, Storage type URL, Interface URL and Processes URL even when the Task store is MongoDB or MCP.
artifacts.identity_strategy: The bootstrap file is identified by the reserved filename AGENTS.md in the Task package; it does not replace the Task master-system identifier.

artifacts.name: Interoperability crosswalk
artifacts.description: Declared field and state mappings to FHIR Task, VTODO, WS-HumanTask, schema.org Action and Microsoft todoTask.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Identify by source model, target model and crosswalk version.

functions.name: Create Task
functions.description: Create a Task instance from a definition, request, list or ad-hoc instruction, assigning identifiers and initial status.
inputs: optional requester, requested performers and owner
preconditions: Caller is authorized to create in the target list, project or work-order context
If restriction is supplied, the Task is a fulfill Task and focus is present
effects: A Task record exists in a non-terminal state such as draft, requested, ready or created
Identity mappings are written
Lifecycle history records a creation event with event time and ingestion time

functions.name: Claim or assign Task
functions.description: Move a Task from a potential-owner queue to an actual owner by claim, nomination or direct assignment.
outputs: Status such as received, accepted, reserved or ready
preconditions: Actor is a potential owner and not an excluded owner, or an authorized administrator is assigning
Task is in a claimable non-terminal state
effects: Actual owner is set
Potential owners may lose exclusive claim rights depending on policy
History records the claim or assignment event

functions.name: Start Task
functions.description: Mark that the owner has begun work, recording execution start as event time.
preconditions: Actor is the actual owner or an authorized delegate
Required inputs that must be present are available unless explicitly waived
effects: Status becomes in progress
executionPeriod.start is set as event time
lastModified is set as observation time

functions.name: Complete Task
functions.description: Record successful completion, outputs, outcome and completion event time.
preconditions: Task is in progress or otherwise completable
Composite completion conditions, if any, are satisfied
effects: Status becomes completed
Outputs are stored for downstream Tasks
Parent rollup may be re-evaluated

functions.name: Cancel, fail, reject or enter-in-error
functions.description: Terminate abnormally, distinguish external cancellation, execution failure, pre-start rejection and never-valid entered-in-error.
preconditions: Cancel and fail apply to non-terminal states except where policy allows entered-in-error on any state
Caller has requester, owner or administrator authority as required
effects: Task becomes terminal on the declared path
Children may be cancelled when policy cascades
History records the terminal event and reason

functions.name: Suspend, resume or stop
functions.description: Pause work, resume in the prior state, or stop an in-progress Task back to ready for reassignment or retry.
preconditions: Task is in a non-terminal state for suspend
Stop is from in-progress to ready
effects: Suspend sets on-hold or equivalent and suspends children
Resume restores prior state and resumes children
Stop returns the Task to ready without losing identity

functions.name: Delegate or forward Task
functions.description: Transfer potential or actual ownership to another person or group without creating a new Task identity.
outputs: Updated potential owners or actual owner
preconditions: Source actor is actual owner, stakeholder or administrator as specified by the people-assignment policy
Target is not an excluded owner
effects: Assignment record is rewritten
History records delegation or forwarding
Status may return to ready if the current owner stopped work

functions.name: Escalate on timeout
functions.description: When a deadline is missed, notify stakeholders or administrators and optionally reassign or raise priority.
preconditions: Task definition or instance declares a timeout
effects: Escalation history is appended
Notifications may be sent as sibling one-way objects, not as new Task instances unless the Dimension models them as Tasks

composition.purpose: Record optional containing project. Project contains tasks; this model does not own project, work-package or portfolio semantics.
Record the work order that authorizes and groups operational tasks without absorbing work-order commercial or maintenance semantics.
Reference an independently versioned plan, schedule, ActivityDefinition, BPMN process or PROV Plan that the Task instantiates or follows.
Composite Tasks contain child Task instances with independently tracked status; checklist items may be subordinate rather than child Tasks.
Requester, owner, performers, potential owners, excluded owners, stakeholders and administrators are references to agent master data.
Principal or virtual place of performance is a location reference, not a nested location model.
Align identifiers, status, intent, assignment, basedOn versus focus, periods, restriction, inputs and outputs. Do not claim FHIR conformance.
Align UID, SUMMARY, STATUS, DUE, DTSTART, COMPLETED, PERCENT-COMPLETE, PRIORITY, CLASS, RRULE, ATTACH, RELATED-TO and VALARM. VTODO cannot nest.
Align definition versus instance, generic human roles, claim, delegate, forward, composite tasks, escalation and history. Notifications remain out of scope.
Align agent, object, participant, instrument, location, startTime, endTime, result, error and actionStatus as a web-action view of a Task.
Align performing work with Activity, used and generated entities, associated agents, delegation and optional Plan without treating every PROV Activity as a Task.
Align personal-productivity projection including unstable list-scoped id, waitingOnOthers, deferred, checklistItems and linkedResources.

owner_package_requirements: Designate a Dimension owner package that names the system of record for Task master-system identifiers and the policy for assigning Dimension UUID or ULID surrogates when those identifiers are missing or unstable.
Publish namespace IRIs for Task instances, Task definitions and status alignment maps under the adopting Dimension, without treating a date as an identifier.
Declare which sibling models are required references (Agent at minimum; Project, Work order, Plan, Location as applicable) and which FHIR, VTODO, WS-HumanTask or Graph projections are enabled.
Provide AGENTS.md in every Task package, including MongoDB collections and MCP servers, so agents can locate specification, storage type, interface and processes.
dimension.namespace_guidance: Use a Dimension-owned HTTP IRI base for Task instances and definitions. Do not reuse FHIR resource ids, iCalendar UIDs or Graph todoTask ids as the IRI path unless they are confirmed stable master-system identifiers. Keep status, priority and confidentiality codes in named vocabularies rather than free text.

canonicalization_rules: Canonical Task identity is the master-system identifier; additional business identifiers, UIDs and IRIs are aliases.
Canonical timestamps are RFC 3339 with seconds and an explicit offset or Z.
Native status, priority and confidentiality codes are preserved alongside mapped canonical values; mappings are labeled alignments.
basedOn and focus are distinct references and must not be collapsed.
partOf forms a strict hierarchy; cycles are rejected.
patch_rules: Patches must not replace the master-system identifier.
Status patches must include a reason when moving to failed, cancelled, rejected, on-hold, deferred or entered-in-error.
authoredOn is immutable after create; lastModified is updated on every successful patch and must be greater than or equal to authoredOn.
Intent is immutable on FHIR-shaped instances; a new Task is created if intent changes.
Child cascade of suspend and resume is applied as a single patch set with per-child history events.
compatibility_rules: Consumers must accept unknown native status codes by retaining them and mapping to a canonical unknown or other state rather than dropping the Task.
A Dimension that enables Graph projection must tolerate identifier re-key on list move by preserving the Dimension UUID or ULID.
Absence of VTODO nesting must not be used to forbid FHIR or WS-HumanTask subtasks in other projections.
No projection may claim FHIR, iCalendar, WS-HumanTask or schema.org conformance unless a separate evidence artifact demonstrates it.

identity_priority: UUID or ULID assigned by the adopting Dimension
artifact_rules.timestamp_rule: All Task time values use RFC 3339 with seconds and an explicit numeric offset or Z. Record event time (when work started, ended, fell due, completed, failed or was cancelled) separately from observation or ingestion time (authoredOn, lastModified, DTSTAMP, bodyLastModified) whenever those differ.
artifact_rules.serial_naming_rule: Serial artifact names are {task-master-id}/{artifact-kind}/{artifact-id} with lower-kebab-case kinds. Occurrence dates must not appear as identity segments.
artifact_rules.integrity_rule: Each serial artifact records a checksum or content hash, producer agent, event time and ingestion time. Attachments and evidence packs are immutable once checksummed; replacements create a new artifact identifier.

policies: Least-privilege access by generic human role: potential owners see queue fields; actual owners update execution fields; requesters may cancel according to policy; stakeholders and business administrators may escalate; excluded owners are denied claim and start.

Retain terminal Task records and lifecycle history for the Dimension retention period unless a legal hold applies; entered-in-error records are retained because they may have been used, but must be labeled so they are not treated as valid work.
Treat external standards as alignments. Store native codes and declared maps; do not overwrite native status with a canonical code.
Cascade suspend and resume to children unless a child is already terminal. Do not auto-complete a parent solely because one child completed unless a completion condition says so.

read: Return identity, native and canonical status, assignment, temporal bounds and focus without requiring the caller to understand a particular file format.
Support queue queries by owner, requested performer, status, due window, beneficiary and group identifier.
Include or link relevant history and evidence according to the caller's access scope.
create: Require a title or code and a master-system identifier or a request to mint a Dimension UUID or ULID.
Set authored-on observation time; do not use that timestamp as an identifier.
Reject restriction without fulfill intent and focus.
Optionally bind instantiatesCanonical or instantiatesUri to a definition.
update: Allow owner, status, inputs, outputs, notes, attachments, due times and people assignments under role checks.
Refuse intent mutation on immutable instances.
Record lastModified as observation time and append a history event with event time.
Recompute parent completion conditions when children change.
delete: Prefer terminal cancellation or entered-in-error over physical delete while retention applies.
Physical delete or anonymize only after retention expiry and absence of legal hold, including attachments and renderings.
If a Graph-shaped identifier changed on list move, delete must target the current master-system identifier and the stable Dimension UUID or ULID.

roles.name: Dimension Task steward
responsibilities: Own the Task package, namespaces, status alignment maps and AGENTS.md
Decide master-system versus Dimension surrogate identity policy

roles.name: Requester
responsibilities: Create Tasks and supply basedOn, focus, due window and reason
Cancel requested work according to policy

roles.name: Actual owner
responsibilities: Perform or supervise the work, update progress, inputs and outputs, and complete or fail the Task

roles.name: Business administrator or stakeholder
responsibilities: Oversee outcome, resolve missed deadlines, forward or reassign, and authorize exceptions

roles.name: Agent operator
responsibilities: Execute only legal operations for the current state and role
Preserve native codes and RFC 3339 timestamps with separate event and observation times

access.default_rule: Deny by default. Grant read and update from explicit generic human roles, security labels and beneficiary compartment rules; never infer access solely from possession of a due date or title.
exceptions: Entered-in-error Tasks remain readable to auditors and original requesters but are excluded from work queues.
Legal hold suspends deletion even when retention has expired.
Excluded owners are denied claim, start and complete even if they can read a redacted queue item.
Confidential CLASS or equivalent labels restrict title and body from unprivileged list views.
audit_requirements: Record actor, role, operation, Task identifier, event time and ingestion time for create, claim, assign, start, complete, cancel, fail, enter-in-error, delegate, forward, escalate, suspend, resume and delete.
Retain audit records at least as long as the Task evidence pack.

read_order: Processes URL for claim, start, complete and escalate

coverage.claim: This candidate model covers the defensible operating surface of a format-neutral Task work item using primary sources from HL7, IETF, OASIS, Schema.org, Microsoft, OMG, W3C and ISO public terms. It is an alignment union, not a claim of universal completeness or of conformance to any one standard.

checklist.notes: Master-system identifier, business identifiers, group identifier, iCalendar UID, governed IRI and Dimension UUID or ULID, with Graph re-key on list move documented.

FHIR twelve-state set, iCalendar four-state VTODO, schema.org four-state Action, Graph five-state including waitingOnOthers and deferred, plus WS-HumanTask claim, delegate, forward, skip and escalation.
basedOn, focus, beneficiary, requester, owner, performers, potential and excluded owners, RELATED-TO, linkedResources, project, work order and plan references.
Requested, due, execution, completed, authored, last modified, recurrence, reminders and RFC 3339 event versus observation time.
relevantHistory, WS-HumanTask task events, PROV association, attribution, delegation, used and generated entities.
Requester versus owner versus actual owner versus stakeholders and business administrators.
FHIR restriction invariant, lastModified versus authoredOn, legal operations by state, composite completion conditions.
Role-based default deny, CLASS confidentiality, excluded owners, beneficiary compartment and audit of lifecycle operations.
Retention after terminal state, legal hold, entered-in-error retention because the record may have been used, and attachment disposal.
Declared alignments to FHIR Task, VTODO, WS-HumanTask, schema.org Action, PROV-O and Microsoft todoTask without conformance claims.
Competing priority scales and FHIR immutable intent are modeled as alignments.
partOf, composite and ad-hoc subtasks, checklists, non-nesting VTODO and completion conditions.
Registry factor_robotics is 0.00. No primary robotics tasking standard was incorporated; robot work cells and mission tasks remain an omission.

known_omissions: Full ISO 21502:2020 clauses beyond the public work-package definition remain paywalled.
BPMN 2.0.2 Task types (user, service, script, manual, business-rule, send, receive) were not read from the normative PDF and are not treated as canonical here.
OSLC Change Management, IHE XDW, JSCalendar Task conversion, RFC 5546 iTIP scheduling and CalDAV access protocols were not fetched.
IETF draft-okutomi-agent-human-interaction is emerging and not used as a primary source.
Military METL, legal obligation tasks, education assignments and GTD personal-productivity methods lack primary support in this pack.
No single global Task IRI registry exists.
Percent-complete semantics under composite routing patterns are only sketched from WS-HumanTask completion conditions.
conflicts: Status vocabularies conflict: FHIR twelve codes versus VTODO four versus ActionStatusType four versus Graph five versus WS-HumanTask richer human-task states. Native codes are retained.
Priority scales conflict: FHIR routine/urgent/asap/stat versus iCalendar 0-9 versus Graph low/normal/high versus WS-HumanTask integer priority.
Identifier stability conflicts: Graph todoTask id changes when moved between lists; FHIR Resource.id is assigned once; iCalendar UID is required and persistent.
Hierarchy conflicts: VTODO cannot nest; FHIR partOf and WS-HumanTask composite tasks allow children.

Intent-versus-event: FHIR Task spans intent and event; schema.org Action and PROV Activity describe occurrences; a proposal Task is not the same individual as its later execution record if intent is immutable.
Homonym: Amazon ECS task is a compute unit, not this work-item Task.
regional_assumptions: Healthcare examples (encounter, beneficiary, insurance) follow HL7 FHIR and are optional outside clinical Dimensions.
Confidentiality CLASS follows iCalendar PUBLIC/PRIVATE/CONFIDENTIAL; regional privacy law (for example GDPR erasure versus audit retention) is a Dimension policy overlay, not a universal Task rule.
WS-HumanTask people assignment assumes an organizational directory whose schema is out of scope.
Time zones in Graph dateTimeTimeZone must be projected to RFC 3339 instants with explicit offset or Z for canonical storage.
adversarial_checks: If a consumer treats lastModified or due date as the Task identifier, identity policy is violated.
If basedOn and focus are collapsed, fulfillment authorization is mis-attributed.
If entered-in-error is physically deleted immediately, FHIR retention rationale that the Task may have been used is violated.
If VTODO non-nesting is used to reject FHIR subtasks, a projection rule has been mistaken for a Task semantic.
If Graph waitingOnOthers or deferred is dropped because FHIR lacks those codes, a rare lifecycle path is lost.
If notifications are stored as Tasks without a one-way flag, WS-HumanTask notification semantics are violated.
If a Dimension claims FHIR or iCalendar conformance from this alignment union, the claim is unsupported.
